paragraphs: Rabbi Yehoshua ben Gamla: Yuchasin, in the sequence of tannaim under Chananyah ben Chizkiyah, writes that he married Marta bat Boethus. In Eichah Rabbah, the section ‘For these things I weep,’ she is called Miriam bat Boethus; see there about her wealth. She was a widow and very rich. Before he married her, she gave King Yannai a tarkav of dinars so that he would make him high priest: Yoma 18a. See Rashi and Tosafot there: this is not the King Yannai near the beginning of the chapter HaOmer in Kiddushin, 66a, who killed Israel’s sages, for he himself was high priest and would not have appointed another in his place. So too Tosafot Yeshanim 8b. In the Mishnah, Yevamot 61a: Yehoshua ben Gamla betrothed her, then became high priest, then married her. In Sukkah 52b: Marta bat Boethus’s son—he was a priest, Rashi. He did good for Israel by instituting teachers for children: Bava Batra 21a, ‘May he be remembered for good.’ In the Mishnah, the chapter Amar Lahem HaMemunneh, the lots had been made of boxwood, and he made them of gold; they would mention him with praise. Tosafot in Bava Batra cited above write that he was completely righteous; the statement in Yevamot, ‘I see a conspiracy here,’ was because there were others more distinguished than he. Ritva writes in Yoma that he subsequently made himself worthy; some say that there were two such men. One may further say that he was pious and worthy, but that there was another priest greater than he in wisdom and in number, or in one of these. Rabbi Eliezer ben Yaakov asked him, Yehoshua bar Mammal, and Yonatan ben Meshullam.
